summary: CCM supports H004 (coupled hemispheric oscillator): bidirectional causal manifold coupling where SH's manifold contains more information about NH dynamics (ρ_max=0.401) than NH about SH (ρ_max=0.204). The stronger SH→NH attractor coupling is consistent with the SH acting as the 'memory' component of the coupled oscillator — SH's larger ocean area provides a more complete representation of the joint attractor. NH drives the global mean more strongly (NH→global ρ=0.776 vs SH→global ρ=0.667), suggesting NH is the primary driver of global mean variability while SH is the slower, memory-carrying component.
